clue.text: Initially dislodged, small girl back on bed below?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it, so the girl comes second
the opening letter is knocked out of place, so the first letter of the next word goes

parts.note: baby as an adjective means small, as in baby carrots

indicators.note: going back means the word girl stands for is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A small girl, startled out of place, turns over in a bed where something is hidden underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: BABY loses its B to give ABY, then LASS reversed adds SSAL: ABYSSAL. The question mark flags the definition as an oblique one.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssal describes the deepest ocean zone, so the sea floor far down in the depths is fairly called an abyssal bed lying below.

clue.text: Acknowledge Charlie seen in fantastic part

indicators.note: something seen in another sits inside it, so the Charlie letter goes into the next word

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent or fantastic
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
PT is the standard abbreviation for part

explanation.surface: Someone admits that Charlie appeared in a wonderful role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a role in a play, but it is only its two-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept a point is to recognise or concede it, which is what acknowledging it means.

clue.text: 50 housed in the old squat finding chicken

parts.note: ye is the archaic spelling of the

indicators.note: something housed in a building is held within it, so the number goes inside the other letters

parts.note: squat means short and low to the ground
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people are living in an old squat, where they come across a chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads squat as an occupied building, but here it is the adjective meaning short and low.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken and yellow are both informal words for cowardly, so one adjective substitutes for the other.

clue.text: One growing up as prison child

parts.note: a stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A youngster raised behind bars, growing up as a prison child.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalagmite is a mineral column that builds upward from a cave floor, so it literally grows up over time.

clue.text: What was tender of Italians welcoming British stars?

indicators.note: a host welcoming a guest takes them in, so the outer word holds the British letter

parts.note: the lira was Italy's currency, legal tender before the euro
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A question about what Italians once used as money, with Britain somehow part of the picture of the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like a feeling or a person who tends, but it is legal tender, i.e. money.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra is a constellation of the zodiac, a named group of stars representing the scales.

clue.text: Long cushion provides help

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long, firm pillow laid across a bed
second meaning: to support or prop up

explanation.surface: A long cushion turns out to be a comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for an elongated pillow and also a verb meaning to support or reinforce, so it serves as help.

clue.text: Dashing young men very attractive in red

parts.note: bloods is an old word for fashionable young men about town
hot is slang for very attractive

explanation.surface: Handsome young men look very attractive dressed in red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' reads as a colour of clothing, but it describes eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodshot eyes are reddened by swollen blood vessels, so the adjective describes eyes that look red.

clue.text: Gospeller to one side has small guitar

parts.note: one side is left, abbreviated L
uke is short for ukulele, a small four-stringed guitar

explanation.surface: An evangelist stands off to the side holding a ukulele.
explanation.definitionFit: Luke is one of the four evangelists credited with writing a Gospel of the New Testament.

clue.text: Female coming in hates crappy cricket series

indicators.note: something coming in enters, so the female word goes inside the next word
crappy means badly made, so the combined letters are rebuilt in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman joins the crowd and declares that she hates a dismal run of cricket matches.
explanation.walkthrough: The female goes in first, then the whole lot is rearranged. The Ashes is the Test series played between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashes is the famous recurring contest of Test matches between England and Australia, so it is a cricket series.

clue.text: Communist not best pleased in humanitarian group

parts.note: red is the usual shorthand for a communist
cross means annoyed, i.e. not best pleased

explanation.surface: An irritated communist finds himself in an aid organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is the international relief organisation that helps victims of war and disaster.

clue.text: Odds of criminal receiving fifty lashes?

indicators.note: a word receiving something takes it in, so the number goes inside
the odds of a word are its letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and so on

parts.note: letters one, three, five and seven of the word
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer is sentenced to fifty strokes of the whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lashes' looks like a flogging; the question mark signals the other sense, eyelashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cilia are eyelashes in anatomical Latin, and the word also covers the tiny hairlike filaments on cells.

clue.text: Stop boss being an idiot

parts.note: to block is to stop
the head is the boss

explanation.surface: An employee tries to stop their boss from behaving like a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockhead is a dim-witted, stupid person, so the noun is a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Publicity material has right look reportedly

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: proper means right, and a gander is British slang for a look

explanation.surface: Some promotional literature has the right appearance, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: To have a gander is British slang for to take a look.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is information, often biased, spread to promote a cause, so it is a kind of publicity material.

clue.text: Starts with the straight approach — right for tyrant

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters only

parts.note: the first letter of each of these three words
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Advice on dealing with a despot: begin with an honest, direct approach.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was a Russian emperor with absolute power, and the word is used for any autocratic ruler.

clue.text: Following the mail we get on turning bed

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following
the mail that belongs to us is our post

indicators.note: turning round means the word for on is written back to front

parts.note: re means on or about

explanation.surface: After the mail arrives, we carry on tossing and turning in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' looks like tossing in bed, but it only turns round the little word for on.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-poster is a large bed with a post at each corner, often holding up a canopy.

clue.text: Noble creature with pride beheaded after moving protest

indicators.note: beheading cuts off the top, so the first letter of the creature is removed
one piece placed after another comes second in the answer

parts.note: a march is a protest on the move
a lioness lives in a pride of lions

explanation.surface: A proud aristocratic animal is decapitated following a violent demonstration, like a scene from a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' looks like vanity but is the name for a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchioness is a woman holding the rank of marquess, or a marquess's wife, so she is a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Game girl brought up in a mythical land

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union
Rita is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up a word means it reads from the bottom upward

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sporty young woman was raised in a fairy-tale country.
explanation.walkthrough: RU and RITA, then IN brought up to give NI, then A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the imaginary central European kingdom in Anthony Hope's novel The Prisoner of Zenda, a fictional country.

clue.text: Meringue ingredient for example affected weight

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for for example

indicators.note: something affected has been altered, so the letters of the word for heaviness are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A baker worries that one meringue component has changed the weight of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Meringue is made by whisking the clear albumen of eggs with sugar, so this is its main component.

clue.text: People with key arrive outside to open

indicators.note: the verb for arriving sits outside, wrapping round the other pieces

parts.note: to come is to arrive
men are people
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: People holding a key turn up outside a door to unlock it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' and 'open' suggest a lock, but the key is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: To open proceedings is to begin them, and commence is a formal verb for beginning.

clue.text: Spirit behind someone else's work?

parts.note: surface reading: a phantom haunting the background of another person's creation
setter's reading: the spirit is a phantom, and a phantom author writes books credited to someone else

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like the driving force or inspiration behind a project, but it is the hidden author.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostwriter is a hired author who writes speeches, books or articles published under another person's name.

clue.text: One needing rest in Greek character's location

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so these pieces go within the Greek letter

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
I is the Roman numeral for one
to lie down is to rest

explanation.surface: Someone in need of a lie-down finds it in a Greek's place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' sounds like a person from Greece, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is a person's surroundings or social setting, so it is a kind of place or location.

clue.text: Something added is a letter dictated

indicators.note: dictated words are spoken out for someone to write, so it is their sound that counts

parts.note: a single letter of the alphabet, the twenty-fourth one, spoken with its article

explanation.surface: A postscript is a letter dictated to a secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like correspondence being dictated; it is the alphabet letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extension to a building or an addition to a document, so it is a thing appended.

clue.text: Wife to independent politician being spineless sort

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
I is the abbreviation for independent
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A wife is married to a non-party politician who is a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a weak, feeble or timid person, someone without courage or backbone.

clue.text: Loud Welshwoman entertains singer keeping time

indicators.note: a host who entertains someone has them inside the house, so her name holds the rest

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh girl's name

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it, so the singer encloses the time letter

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A noisy woman from Wales plays host to a vocalist who keeps the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: time goes inside the singer, and that goes inside the Welsh name.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentorian means extremely powerful in voice, after Stentor, the herald in the Iliad whose voice equalled fifty men.

clue.text: Relative close to collapse in pleasant surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings enclose what lies in them, so the adjective wraps around the single letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A family member is near to breaking down despite being in a comfortable setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister, so she is a family member.

clue.text: Old-fashioned loyalty not hard for left-winger

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for hard is taken away

parts.note: troth is an archaic word for faithfulness, as in plighting one's troth
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Traditional loyalty isn't difficult for a socialist.
explanation.walkthrough: TROTH minus H.
explanation.definitionFit: Trot is informal for a Trotskyist, a follower of Leon Trotsky, and so a member of the far left.

clue.text: Canoeing recklessly across river shows unawareness

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so the scrambled letters stretch around the river
doing something recklessly means wildly and without order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Paddling carelessly over a river reveals that someone has no idea of the danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is lack of knowledge or information, the state of not being aware of something.

clue.text: Public rights guardian bans one Parisian race

indicators.note: banning something keeps it out, so the French word is removed from the official's title

parts.note: a tribune in ancient Rome was elected to protect the rights of the common people
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A civil-rights watchdog prohibits a person from Paris from running in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIBUNE minus UN. 'Race' suggests a contest, but it means a people.
explanation.definitionFit: A race in the older sense is a people of shared descent, and a tribe is such a group.

clue.text: Complex woman drops ecstasy into claret when sloshed

indicators.note: dropping something into a drink puts it inside, so the drug letter goes into the wine
sloshed means drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A complicated woman slips a pill into her red wine once she is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' reads as complicated, but it points to the Electra complex in psychoanalysis.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is the Greek tragic heroine whose name Jung gave to a daughter's attachment to her father, the Electra complex.

clue.text: Whilst travelling north, hiding amongst Europeans

indicators.note: something amongst others sits in their midst, so these pieces go between the two European letters

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, twice for the plural
N is the abbreviation for north
a hiding is a thrashing or heavy defeat, as is a rout

explanation.surface: On a journey north, someone conceals themselves among fellow Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' suggests concealment, but it is a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: En route is a French phrase meaning on the way, so it describes someone in the course of a journey.
